# CS-007: The firewall bouncer also protects Docker published ports

- **Group:** CrowdSec and fail2ban
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

Docker published ports are forwarded, not delivered to INPUT, so a firewall bouncer hooked only into INPUT never filters traffic to containers. Without a tunnel, published containers are exactly what scanners hit. The bouncer must also hook DOCKER-USER (iptables) or the forward hook (nftables). This is read from the live rules, not the bouncer config (which holds the API key).

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER | grep -i crowdsec; sudo nft list tables | grep crowdsec
```

## How to fix it

Add DOCKER-USER to iptables_chains (or forward to nftables_hooks) in the firewall bouncer config, then restart the bouncer

## What a fix can break

Banned addresses also lose access to containers, which is the point.
